newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 4.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- The Bank of Korea said the year- on-year growth rate of M2, which comprises cash in circulation plus demand and savigs deposits at banks stood at 20.5 percent in March on an averaged outstanding basis, the highest since the 20.8 percent rate recorded back in October 1993.

- Local civic groups called on the United States and the European Union to stop interfering in internal affairs while accusing them of unjustifiably finding fault with the nation's frugality campaign.
- Escapees from North Korea have formed a group of anti-Kim Jong-il resistance fighters in China.
- Foreign Universities will be allowed to open branch campuses in 1998.
- The Organizaiotn for Economic Cooperation and Development is planning to propel international agreement about freeing domestic investment of foreingers.

- South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor Co would reduce procution by four hours a day from April 8-12, largely because of rising inventory. Other carmakers have no immediate plan to cut production but they are also under pressure from growing inventories.
- The South Korean government is considering comprehensive counterplan to reduce travel deficit.
